stories.title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others
stories.simple_summary: Many tech companies, including Monday.com, have laid off workers and said it was because of AI. The article lists 20 companies that have done this.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business using tech tools, this shows the market is changing quickly — but most small business AI tools are still being built and improved, so it's worth watching what happens next.

stories.title: What's the difference between closed, open‑source and open-weight AI? A researcher explains
stories.simple_summary: The article explains the differences between three types of AI: closed AI (a company controls it completely), open-source AI (the recipe is public and anyone can modify it), and open-weight AI (the instructions are published but with some restrictions).
stories.why_it_matters: Understanding these differences helps you know how much control companies have over AI and whether it's truly transparent or not — useful for deciding which AI tools to trust for your business.

stories.title: Librarians are hosting viral ‘Avoiding AI’ workshops for people who are fed up with Big Tech
stories.simple_summary: Libraries are running popular workshops called 'Avoiding AI' where many people are showing up to learn how to stay away from AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: People are feeling overwhelmed and want help opting out — this shows you're not alone if you feel frustrated with AI being everywhere.

stories.title: People Are Starting to Record Every Conversation They Have Without Disclosing It, and It's Gross
stories.simple_summary: People are now secretly recording conversations with AI (and possibly other people) without telling anyone it's happening.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a privacy concern — be aware that some conversations might be recorded and stored without your knowledge, and be cautious about what you discuss.

stories.title: Robert Morris University infuses artificial intelligence into MBA curriculum
stories.simple_summary: A university is now teaching AI as part of its MBA (business degree) program to train future business leaders.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about education for young professionals — nothing you need to act on right now, but shows AI is becoming standard business knowledge.

stories.title: One fallen power line exposed a growing AI data center problem. Here’s how to fix it.
stories.simple_summary: AI data centers (huge computer buildings that power AI) had a problem when a power line fell in Virginia, and they weren't prepared to handle the outage well.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a technical issue for engineers and city planners — it doesn't affect you directly, but shows data centers need better emergency backup systems.

stories.title: The AI jobs apocalypse probably isn’t coming anytime soon
stories.simple_summary: Experts say AI probably won't cause a massive sudden loss of jobs across the entire economy in the near future, even though some jobs will change.
stories.why_it_matters: If you worried AI would wipe out entire industries overnight, this research suggests change will be slower and more gradual than the scary headlines suggest.

stories.title: From Silicon Valley to DC, the tech world is suddenly obsessed with one concept in AI: Distillation
stories.simple_summary: Tech companies and government officials are all talking about 'AI distillation' — a technique where you take a big complex AI and shrink it down to work on regular computers.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to tech investors and engineers — but in plain terms, it means AI could eventually run on cheaper equipment, making it more useful for small business.

stories.title: Opinion | The Flawed Environmental Case Against Data Centers
stories.simple_summary: This opinion piece argues that concerns about AI data centers harming the environment may be overstated or based on incomplete information.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an opinion debate among experts — not settled fact — so take environmental claims about AI with some skepticism until more proof arrives.

stories.title: No, OpenAI's models didn't go 'rogue' when they broke into Hugging Face. Here's what really happened.
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI's AI models didn't go 'rogue' or break rules when they accessed a platform called Hugging Face — something else actually happened.
stories.why_it_matters: Stories about AI suddenly acting on its own and breaking rules are scary but usually not accurate — this is a reminder to be skeptical of dramatic headlines.

stories.title: North Carolina teen accused of using AI for sexual exploitation. Are state laws strong enough?
stories.simple_summary: A teenager in North Carolina was accused of using AI to create sexual content to exploit someone, and the article asks whether state laws are tough enough for this crime.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI is being misused by some people for serious harm — it's a real safety issue that parents and communities should be aware of.

stories.title: I tried out OpenAI’s new AI keypad — which will be fun for some coders and slightly mystifying to everyone else
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI made a new tool (an AI keypad) that coders might enjoy using, but most regular people will probably find confusing or not useful.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a new tool for programmers, not for typical small business owners — nothing you need to pay attention to unless you write code.
